subject: Re: Region pinning & data residency — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@acmebank.com>, Sofía Martínez <sofia.martinez@acmebank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region pinning & data residency — follow-up and next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the team. Quick recap and the follow-ups we committed to: 

Summary from today
- Primary requirement: PII and customer-sensitive data must remain in the EU (e.g., eu-west-1).
- DR/Failover: Acme would like cross-region failover to be allowed for service continuity, but only to a limited set of regions (US: us-west-2) and only under documented incident conditions.
- Backups: Encrypted backups and snapshot retention policies — need confirmation on whether backups can live outside EU only for DR and whether those backups must be encrypted with CMK.
- Logging & auditing: Request/response logging, retention period, access controls and audit logs for any access to PII.

Action items for Redwood
1) Provide a short note on how region pinning is enforced (strict pin vs. soft failover), and what guarantees we can provide for no egress under normal operations.
2) Clarify backup placement and encryption options (customer-managed keys supported?).
3) Explain logging behavior: are request/response logs retained by default? how long, and can we disable/obfuscate logs for PII?
4) Share SOC2/Security artifacts and the region-pinning architecture diagram (attachment).

I've attached the Redwood_Data_Residency_Overview.pdf we referenced on the call. Aditya — can you take #1-#3 and share a short technical note + diagram? Vanessa — I'll loop you in for procurement/contract language once we confirm the technical constraints. 

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

- Redwood_Data_Residency_Overview.pdf (pdf)

From: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@acmebank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofía Martínez <sofia.martinez@acmebank.com>, Acme Bank Security <security@acmebank.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Region pinning & data residency — follow-up and next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and for joining the call. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: Correct — all PII and production inference for EU customers must be pinned to eu-west-1. We need contractual language that prevents normal traffic from leaving the EU region.
- Failover: We are open to a DR-only failover path to us-west-2, but it must be a documented, tested process and requires an access/audit trail for any DR activation.
- Backups: Snapshots/backups should remain within the EU unless DR activation occurs. Backups in other regions are acceptable only if encrypted with a customer key and written only after documented mutual approval.
- Logs: We require request/response logging to be optional by route and, when enabled, retained for up to 12 months. Any log access must be auditable and tied to IAM controls.

I've attached our internal security questionnaire with a few fields already filled out — see AcmeBank_Security_Questionnaire.pdf. Can your security/tech team confirm fields related to key management (KMIP/KMS), data-at-rest encryption, and whether you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in EU regions? Also please confirm your RPO/RTO numbers for region failover scenarios.

Sofía — do you want to loop in legal/procurement now or after the technical note?

Thanks,
Daniel Wu
Director, Cloud Security — Acme Bank
daniel.wu@acmebank.com

Attachments:
- AcmeBank_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@acmebank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region pinning & data residency — follow-up and next steps

Hi Daniel — thanks, and great questions. Quick technical notes below addressing each item; happy to hop on a short call to walk through diagrams and configs.

1) Region pinning enforcement- Redwood supports per-account and per-route region pinning. For Acme we can configure a strict pin so that inference requests and any persisted context (KV cache, embeddings stored by the app) are routed only to eu-west-1 under normal operation. Traffic will not egress the pinned region unless an explicit, documented DR failover workflow is executed. 

2) Cross-region failover and DR- We provide a configurable failover policy:
  - Warm standbys: we can maintain warm replicas in us-west-2 but keep them logically isolated (no serving traffic) unless a DR runbook is executed.
  - Failover activation requires multi-party approval (customer + Redwood), is logged, and generates an immutable audit entry.
  - RPO/RTO: typical snapshot-based failover can achieve RPO ~15m and RTO in the 10-30 minute range depending on model size and warm standby configuration. If you need stronger RPO we can discuss synchronous replication patterns but there is a cost/latency tradeoff.

3) Backups and encryption- Snapshots and periodic backups can be kept in-region by default. For DR-only replication to US, we require customer consent and support customer-managed keys (CMK) in EU (we integrate with common KMS providers and support Bring Your Own Key). All backups are AES-256 encrypted at rest; cross-region transfer happens over TLS and with server-side encryption.

4) Logging, retention and PII handling- Default behavior: minimal operational logs retained for 30 days. Request/response logging is off by default for PII-sensitive routes. Options:
  - Route-level logging: enable/disable per route.
  - Redaction: token-level redaction available (PII masking) prior to writing logs.
  - Retention: configurable up to 12 months; we can also push logs to your SIEM or S3 bucket in-region.
  - Access: audit logs for any access to logs/keys, integrated with your IAM.

5) Artifacts and compliance- We can produce SOC 2 artifacts, architecture diagrams, and a short runbook for failover tests. See the attached architecture diagram and this developer doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/platform/region-pinning.

Next steps
- Marissa: will share redlined config language for the contract (no egress guarantee + DR runbook).
- Daniel / Security: if helpful we can schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive next week — propose Tue 20 Apr 2027 10:00 CET (we can convert to your timezone).

I've attached a simple diagram (region-pinning-architecture-diagram.png) and pasted the doc links above. Let me know which specific KMS provider you plan to use and we can provide a short integration checklist.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199
